Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/miked63017__dinolite_uvc_led_control --backend fake on 2026-10-30 07:55 PDT; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper, but the LED, FLC and exposure methods are not on the worker DinoLiteUVCControl; the worker keeps the per-model device objects in ourDevices and the methods live there (dinoliteuvccontrol/dinoliteuvccontrol.py:24-41, README.md:19-25). A family config over the worker cannot reach them, so this package is a decorated direct Driver over the worker (the card decision is direct-driver). The driver reaches the selected device through self.native.ourDevices[0]; this is the only way to use the card's entry symbol, which G7 requires as native. The five G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL warnings are the consequence: the gate Recorder wraps only the worker, so calls on the nested device object are not recorded. The actions are not no-ops: fake.py mirrors the Device0980 object and the package tests show the fake state changes (flc_on, flc_brightness, auto_exposure, exposure_time, main_led_on). The generic UVC standard controls (Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Hue, White Balance, Gamma, Power Line Frequency, Sharpness) are NOT COVERED: their ranges are loaded per model from device0980.json and device0890.json and the two tables differ; the upstream setter reports a rejected value only by printing, so the driver does not invent one range that covers both. The a168:0890 model is covered for the main LED, auto exposure and exposure steps; FLC is not available on that model, so the FLC reads return false or 0 and the FLC actions refuse MHS.DEVICE.PRECONDITION_UNMET. No image capture is exposed because the upstream has no capture API; the clone only controls illumination and exposure. SAFETY: risk R1 from LED illumination (MHS/spec/04-safety.md:67), above the card floor R0. The safe state is all illumination off. The upstream has no device stop: cleanup() is pass and display_shutdown_message() exits the interpreter (dinoliteuvccontrol/dinoliteuvccontrol.py:68-73); native.py's hardware adapter and fake.py implement cleanup() as the illumination-off stop, called by the @estop and by the safe-state action. No independent hardware e-stop is claimed, no hardware was attached, and the hardware path was never run. The 2 s sleep of the upstream toggle_auto_exposure is not reproduced in the fake.
